title: Kashmir
hook: walnuts soaking in pots of water through Shiva's great night, then handed out to the neighbors

segments.voice: Yesterday in Kashmir, the spring at Tulmul, where pilgrims bring rice pudding and read the color of the water.

A kitchen in winter. On a clean cloth, a row of pots, filled to the brim with water, and in the water, walnuts, still in their shells. Someone has drawn on the pots and hung flowers around their necks. The family will sit up with them tonight, singing, worshiping, keeping the lamp going. In a day or two, those walnuts will be soft from the water and on their way to every relative and neighbor on the list. Today, the last of the Kashmir days: Herath, Shiva's great night, kept the Kashmiri way.
screen: `POTS OF WATER AND WALNUTS` → `A NIGHT KEPT AWAKE` → `HERATH`

segments.voice: You met Mahashivaratri in year one: the great night of Shiva, kept with fasting and worship and staying awake. Kashmiri Pandits keep it too, and they call it Herath. In their tradition it's a night kept at home, around the family, more than at a temple. The family sets out a pot and smaller vessels, filled with water and walnuts, and calls the arrangement the vatuk. It's worshiped as Shiva and the company around him. Families tell the meaning in different ways. Some speak of Shiva's wedding to Parvati, with the pots as the wedding guests. Others speak of Bhairava, a fierce form of Shiva, appearing as light. Nobody has to settle it tonight. The water, the flowers and the lamp do their work either way. When the worship is over, the soaked walnuts become prasad, a blessed gift, and they're shared out: to grandparents, to cousins, to the family next door. In the days after, people visit each other with greetings. So the night that begins alone with God ends at other people's doors. And that closes the week: the Varkaris reaching Pandharpur and turning for home, then Kashmir's drained lake, its river of kings, a theater, a recognition, a spring a community watches, and last, a holy night with a kitchen at its center.

segments.voice: Let the room go quiet, the way a house goes quiet late on Herath, and rest your attention on a lamp burning steadily, coming back to it whenever thoughts wander. Near the end, think of three people you'd hand a walnut to, and see each face for one breath. If you pray, you can say om namah shivaya, slowly, under the breath.
Kashmir. Today, Herath, Shiva's great night kept by Kashmiri Pandits, with pots of water and walnuts that become a gift for the neighbors. Today's word.
Your line: Kashmir. A holy night that ends in walnuts carried door to door. That's the week, and day one thousand three hundred ninety-three.
